prompt.context: Our client is a national airline looking to determine the total cost of ice it needs to purchase to serve its customers onboard for the entire fiscal year.
prompt.question: How would you think about calculating the total annual cost of ice for the airline?

clarifying_info.q: How many flights does the airline operate daily?
clarifying_info.a: The airline has 40 one-way flights daily.

clarifying_info.q: How many seats does each flight have?
clarifying_info.a: Each flight has a maximum capacity of 120 passengers.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average occupancy rate?
How many drinks does each customer consume on average?
clarifying_info.a: On average, each customer consumes 1 drink.

clarifying_info.q: How much ice is used per drink / per customer?
clarifying_info.a: A five-pound bag of ice can serve 25 customers.

clarifying_info.q: How much does a five-pound bag of ice cost?

framework: Determine total number of customers served annually (flights × capacity × occupancy × 365 days)
Determine ice consumption per customer (bags of ice per customer, using known bag-to-customer ratio)
Determine cost per unit of ice (cost per bag)
Multiply through: total customers ÷ customers per bag × cost per bag = total annual ice cost

questions.prompt: Calculate the total number of customers served by the airline annually.
questions.guidance: Break into: number of flights per year = 40 × 365 = 14,600. Average passengers per flight = 120 × 80% = 96. Total annual customers = 14,600 × 96 ≈ 1,401,600.

math.setup: Annual flights × avg passengers per flight

questions.prompt: Calculate the total number of 5-pound ice bags needed and the total annual ice cost.
questions.guidance: Each bag serves 25 customers. Total bags = total customers ÷ 25. Total cost = total bags × $15.

recommendation: The airline's total annual ice cost is approximately $840,000, based on ~1.4 million passengers each consuming 1 drink, with a 5-lb bag serving 25 customers at $15 per bag.
risks: Occupancy rate may vary seasonally or by route, affecting actual passenger count
Ice usage could vary by flight duration (longer flights may require more drinks/ice)
Bulk purchasing or supplier contracts could change the per-bag cost
next_steps: Validate assumptions against actual passenger and beverage data
Explore bulk purchasing discounts to reduce the $15/bag cost
Consider whether ice usage differs meaningfully across cabin classes or route types
